page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 8 vCPUs and 30 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:3.75 CPU-to-memory ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, the hardware allocates 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. The cache structure comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include standard AVX, AES, and FMA, whereas modern vectorized formats such as AVX-512 and AMX are unsupported. The instance includes no attached local storage or GPUs, requiring reliance on remote persistent disks for filesystem operations.

Benchmark results place the processor performance in the lower quartiles of contemporary cloud computing instances. Single-thread processing yields a Geekbench score of 923.0 and stress-ng throughput of 1113.08, reflecting bottom-decile single-core metrics. Multi-threaded evaluations show similar limitations, recording 3531.0 on Geekbench and 6656.21 on PassMark CPU. Compression workloads display constrained throughput, registering 19.07 GB/sec on single-threaded gzip and 6.95 GB/sec on single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In contrast, memory bandwidth achieves moderate results on large-block operations, delivering 45.37 GB/sec for uncached reads and 34.65 GB/sec for writes.

Application and system benchmarks reflect standard execution profiles for early-generation general-purpose hardware. Redis throughput delivers 5.27 million SET operations per second, database operations achieve a PassMark score of 2417.61, and static web serving throughput measures 4.56 GB/sec. Small-scale 135M parameter LLM inference achieves 327.51 prompt tokens per second and 100.1 text generation tokens per second. The server trades peak per-core compute capacity for predictable dedicated core access and stable RAM capacity, making it suitable for standard web application hosting, mid-tier background processing, legacy enterprise systems, and lightweight data staging workloads that do not demand advanced vector instructions or local NVMe input-output speeds.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 vCPUs, 30 GB of RAM, and dedicated execution on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz across 4 physical cores. It features 45 MB of L3 cache, basic AVX, and AES hardware acceleration, while omitting AVX-512 support, local storage disks, and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate lower-tier single-core and multi-core computing metrics, with a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and multi-core score of 3531.0, accompanied by constrained compression rates. Uncached memory throughput performs moderately, reaching 45.37 GB/sec read and 34.65 GB/sec write. Application benchmarks show 5.27 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.56 GB/sec web serving throughput. The configuration serves routine general-purpose deployments, such as mid-tier web serving, internal enterprise applications, lightweight databases, and standard background job processing.

tagline: Dedicated Intel Xeon computing with balanced memory capacity for routine web hosting, staging environments, and standard background application processing.
bullet_points: 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores on Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture
30 GB system memory with 45.37 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth
45 MB shared L3 cache with hardware AES and standard AVX support
Zero integrated local disk storage, operating fully via networked storage
Suited for mid-tier web servers, general application backends, and background jobs
